newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria must privatise construction - minister.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria must privatise construction - minister.

text.p: Interim Construction Minister Nikola Karadimov said on Monday Bulgaria should fully privatise its construction sector if it wanted to join the European Union at a later date.
He told a news conference his ministry was speeding up sell-offs and closures demanded by international lenders as a condition for new funding.

"Within the next 10 weeks privatisation procedures for the sale of three cement plants and another 15 firms in the sector should be finalised and another 25 companies will be offered for sale," Karadimov said.
"Ten enterprises, which are already practically closed down, will be liquidated," he added.
The three cement plants earmarked for sale are Zlatna Panega, Beloizvorski Ziment, and Granitoid.
Karadimov said that while the production of construction materials would be partially privatised, the country's construction sector should be fully privatised.
"The current 90 percent state stake (in the construction sector) is a mere absurdity. It should be fully privatised if the country aims to join the European Union," he said.

The caretaker cabinet, which took office on February 13, has as its main task to prepare general elections on April 19, but it is also negotiating with lenders and laying the ground for future reforms.
The World Bank said on Sunday Bulgaria stood to receive a loan of $200 million if it met reform targets. -- Galina Sabeva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
